description: .Net GPU compute for the browser and desktop. Write once, run on WebGPU, WebGL, Wasm, CUDA, OpenCL, and CPU.
releaseNotes: v5.4.51 (forks 2.4.41) - NEW: accelerator.ReclaimableDeviceBytes(), the device memory the registered reclaimers (idle buffer pools) could give back now. v5.4.50 (forks 2.4.40) - NEW: Accelerator.DeviceMemoryBudgetBytes (an application budget for device memory) and Accelerator.AllocatedDeviceBytes; with a budget set, TryGetFreeMemory and the memory-pressure reclaim work on every backend, not only CUDA. NEW: AMD OpenCL reports free device memory. v5.4.49 (forks 2.4.39) - FIX (all backends): a kernel that fails to compile no longer breaks later kernels that call a helper it called (NullReferenceException); its helpers are removed from the context and generated again. v5.4.48 (forks 2.4.38) - FIX (WebGPU): 5.4.47 could leave a generator placeholder in the WGSL ("if (/*__UFIF0__*/) {") of a kernel that returns early on a condition read from a view and later calls a helper that takes a view; Chrome rejected the shader. A placeholder that is still there after generation is now a compile error. v5.4.47 (forks 2.4.38) - FIX (WebGPU): a barrier under a condition read from a view at a group-uniform address (if (n < N) with N from a params view) compiles (Tint treats read_write storage loads as non-uniform; the condition is taken from invocation 0 through workgroupUniformLoad); FIX (WebGPU): no unreachable trailing return (Chrome "code is unreachable" warning) and no stray carriage returns in the generated WGSL. v5.4.46 (forks 2.4.38) - FIX (WebGPU): the same kernel compiled again gives byte-identical WGSL, so the compiled-shader cache and the browser pipeline cache hit (names no longer come from IR node ids); FIX (WebGL): byte-identical GLSL and the same GL program id for the same text (a recompiled kernel no longer links a duplicate program); FIX (all backends): a kernel optimizes the same whatever the context compiled before (IRContext.Optimize optimizes callees before their callers); FIX (all backends): a kernel that fails to compile no longer makes every later new kernel in the context fail (NullReferenceException in IfConversion); its half-built methods are removed. v5.4.45 (forks 2.4.37) - FIX (WebGPU): a dropped kernel is freed (the shader-resolve cache held every dispatched kernel); FIX (Wasm): a worker module-cache flush no longer strands an older live accelerator (Module not cached for kernelId N); NEW (Wasm, WebGL): the shader-artifact cache rebuilds a kernel loaded again (after its owner was collected or after ReleaseCompilerCaches) without IR or code generation; FIX: the artifact cache key includes the context code-generation settings. v5.4.44 (forks 2.4.37) - NEW: accelerator.ReleaseCompilerCaches() releases the context cache of your kernel code after a batch of loads (browser heap); FIX: Context.ClearCache / ReleaseCompilerCaches is thread-safe against kernel loads on other threads (a context-wide compile lock); FIX: the argument mapper type table is locked. v5.4.43 (forks 2.4.36) - FIX (WebGL): buffers are tiled to the device MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE (browsers without a GPU, SwiftShader 8192). v5.4.42 (forks 2.4.36) - FIX: IBrowserMemoryBuffer.CopyToHostUint8ArrayAsync returns an owned copy on Wasm and WebGL. v5.4.41 (forks 2.4.36) - NEW: ArrayView.CopyToHostUint8ArrayAsync(); FIX: MemoryBuffer readbacks accept the native buffer behind a view; Uint8Array readbacks are owned copies on Wasm and WebGL. v5.4.40 (forks 2.4.36) - FIX (browser): reading a view address as long (LoadEffectiveAddressAsPtr) in hot host code could abort the page .NET runtime or return a garbage high word (Mono wasm interpreter conv.i8 bug); the address is now integer arithmetic. v5.4.39 (forks 2.4.35) - FIX (Wasm): a sub-view device copy could throw with a garbage target offset in a busy page. v5.4.38 (forks 2.4.35) - FIX: Math/MathF.Log2, Cbrt, Asinh, Acosh, Atanh compile in kernels (musl libm ports; + IntrinsicMath.Log1P); FIX (WebGPU/WebGL): accurate f32 log/log2/log10; FIX (WebGPU): short-circuit branches meeting before the merge returned 0; PERF: ArgumentMapper no longer blows up browser AOT builds; FIX (WebGPU/WebGL): a call nothing implements fails to compile (was a silent 0). v5.4.37 (forks 2.4.34) - FIX (CUDA): AllocatePageLocked1D / CreatePageLockFromPinned bind the accelerator first (a page lock made off the accelerator's thread threw "invalid device context"); Wasm worker reuses kernel instances across dispatches. v5.4.36 (forks 2.4.33) - PERF (Wasm): a dispatch no longer copies every argument buffer into the linear memory and back out; buffers stay in place between dispatches and are written back only when something needs them (a 64-thread kernel over a 32 MB buffer: 12.5 -> 0.25 ms per launch). v5.4.35 (forks 2.4.33) - FIX (Wasm): disposing a buffer while work queued on it has not run yet no longer fails with RangeError: offset is out of bounds; the buffer is released after that work. v5.4.34 (forks 2.4.33) - FIX (WebGPU / WebGL): MathF.Sin / Cos / Tan accurate at any argument up to 102943 (were 2.7e-4 off at |x| = 2000; now within 1.2e-7 like CUDA / OpenCL / Wasm). PERF (CPU accelerator): a launch of a kernel with barriers or shared memory no longer wakes every runtime thread (about 15 ms per launch -> 1.7 ms for one group). FIX (all backends but Wasm; wrong rounding): a double converted to Half / bf16 / FP8 / FP4 rounds once, to the nearest value of the type, as System.Half does (was rounded to float first). FIX (WebGPU / WebGL Dekker and Ozaki doubles): a double outside the f32 range loaded with a wrong exponent (1e-300 as 1.6e-38); WebGPU doubles below 2^-79 lost their low 29 bits; (float)-0.0 was +0; a double at the f32 overflow edge became NaN; Ozaki (float)d tied the wrong way just past an f32 midpoint. PlaywrightMultiTest honors a test's declared timeout. v5.4.33 (forks 2.4.32) - FIX (CUDA, OpenCL, WebGPU, WebGL, Wasm; silent wrong results): a conversion into bf16, FP8 E4M3 / E5M2 or FP4 E2M1 rounds to the type (was the identity: (float)(BFloat16)x returned x). FIX (same backends; silent wrong results): Half / bf16 / FP8 / FP4 arithmetic results round to the type as the .NET operators do (were float-exact until a store; up to 4,085 of 4,096 Half products differed). FIX (WebGPU): emulated-f16 float -> Half rounds; native f16 division matches .NET. FIX (WebGL): FP8 / FP4 decoders keep -0. OpenCL: a kernel that fails to compile carries the build log in CLException. New tests on every backend: LowPrecisionRoundTrip_*, LowPrecisionArithmetic_*. See CHANGELOG.md.
